dependency: The preferred operating dependency is numbered open trays with self-service shelf return, followed by shared-mat reconciliation. Exact twelve-counter issue is necessary under C1; retaining this particular return arrangement is a preference, not an established causal necessity. The causal_return_path_hypothesis proposes delayed borrower placement (H1), cross-loan or volunteer redistribution (H2), or count error (H3); the recorded recoveries establish none. Reverse the suggested causal arrow as well: a recorded shortage may trigger searching and volunteer redistribution, thereby producing the apparent later recovery, rather than a delayed borrower return causing the earlier shortage. Alternatively, checkout pressure may cause both hurried counts and redistribution. These reversed accounts are hypotheses, not observed causes.

predictions.account: H1: a borrower returns the final counter after placing the tray.
predictions.when: During the one additional twenty-minute block, prospectively select an ordinary return and an intervention return before either occurs. For the intervention only, direct loose counters into that loan's numbered tray instead of the communal intake mat; retain the open tray and self-service shelf. Keep the same planned initial borrower demand, checkout eligibility, and five-minute use allowance. One volunteer watches placement order with the stopwatch while the second independently counts the selected tray. Observe only one selected return at a time, recording early and later counts through at most five minutes.
predictions.result: If H1 operates in a watched ordinary return, a counter should be seen arriving from that borrower after tray placement and before any volunteer transfer; independently agreed counts should rise following that documented arrival. Under the direct-to-own-tray intervention, the corresponding late arrival should occur in the tray without communal-mat recovery. Such an event would support H1 for that watched loan; absence in this small sample would not disprove H1.

predictions.account: H2: handling or borrower traffic redistributes counters across loans.
predictions.when: Apply the same prospectively selected direct-to-own-tray return intervention while logging the intake-mat and selected-tray counts, witnessed transfers, active loans, waiting borrowers, and time remaining. Preserve initial demand and the unchanged availability and five-minute reconciliation target. For the selected return, defer unobserved mat-to-tray supplementation until the timed and independent counts are recorded, and never issue an eleven-counter tray.
predictions.result: If communal redistribution generates apparent recoveries, witnessed mat or other-tray handling should precede those recoveries in the ordinary return; routing the intervention loan directly to its own tray should reduce that particular exchange path. A loose mat counter without a witnessed origin cannot establish correction of the selected loan. A remaining independently verified shortage would therefore remain unresolved evidence rather than become evidence of delayed return. Any apparent improvement is a hypothesis pending observation and may also reflect changed attention.

predictions.account: H3: single-person starting or return counts are erroneous.
predictions.when: Have both volunteers separately count the prospectively selected tray before checkout and on its first return inspection, without sharing their counts first. Record disagreements and timing; do not decide that either volunteer is correct merely because their count is preferred. Fit these checks into the forty volunteer-minutes and keep at most one tray aside.
predictions.result: If count error explains a selected anomaly, separate counts may disagree before any physical transfer, or a repeated agreed count may already be twelve without an arriving counter. Agreement on twelve at checkout followed by agreement on eleven before any transfer would weaken a pure counting-error account for that event, although shared mistakes and the original unverified counts remain possible.

predictions.account: Reversed arrow: a shortage report causes corrective handling and apparent recovery; pressure may also cause both the report and handling.
predictions.when: For each watched selected return, record tray placement, both initial counts, borrower counter arrival, volunteer search, volunteer transfer, and later counts in seconds. Intervene on the return link by withholding undocumented communal-mat supplementation until those observations are recorded; preserve demand, the five-minute loan allowance, and the valued outcome as targets. Finish or record failure by five minutes rather than extend the observation window to manufacture success.
predictions.result: If shortage-triggered handling creates apparent recovery, the shortage report should precede the search and transfer, and the agreed tray count should rise only after a documented volunteer move. An observed borrower-origin arrival before search would instead support the forward H1 account for that loan. If waiting borrowers and low ready-kit counts precede both hurried counts and handling, that pattern is compatible with the pressure account but is not causal proof: demand is held fixed, not independently manipulated. The return-link intervention can test dependence on redistribution, but its effect alone cannot establish counter ownership or exclude altered attention.

surviving_outcome: Retain the valued outcome: explain intermittent short returns sufficiently to choose a bounded change that keeps at least five complete twelve-counter kits available and reconciles each returned loan within five minutes of placement. Seventy-one accounted counters can constitute at most five complete kits plus eleven counters; no sixth complete kit or spare counter can be assumed. The investigation must never issue an incomplete kit, interrupt an active loan, shorten its allowance, or hold more than one tray aside. Direct-to-own-tray return is a candidate intervention that might preserve the outcome while changing the return link; its success is unobserved, and an unresolved shortage at five minutes counts against the target. Necessity of twelve counters follows from the constraint; necessity of the preferred return dependency and achievement of the whole outcome do not follow from the existing record.
unknowns: Which loan supplied each previously found loose counter remains unknown because their origins were unwitnessed and individual counters are indistinguishable.
The original starting and return counts have no independent accuracy check; separate new counts may disagree or share error.
The unresolved counter location and the cause of closing-time concentration remain unknown.

The precise next-block demand and checkout schedule are unspecified; predeclare and hold the intended schedule fixed across the selected returns, recording deviations rather than assuming six historical loans imply identical future traffic.

Whether the valued availability target refers to the complete circulating kit pool or to five simultaneously ready shelf kits needs operational clarification; five circulating complete kits does not establish five ready kits during active loans.
A twenty-minute block may contain too few watched short returns to distinguish the rival accounts, and intervention attention or compliance may change alongside return routing.
The proposed return-link intervention has not demonstrated preservation of either availability or five-minute reconciliation.
